newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Palestinians set up joint commission.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Palestinians set up joint commission.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat agreed on Monday to set up a joint commission that will meet several times a year, make sure each side is meeting its commitments and move relations forward, the State Department said.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns likened the commission to bodies established between the United States and several other countries, including Russia and South Africa.
"Secretary Albright takes this very seriously as a commitment she is making to Chairman Arafat and he to her...to make sure this relationship works well," Burns said of the joint commission.
He spoke after Albright and Arafat held a one-hour meeting and then a working lunch at the State Department after talks between Arafat and President Bill Clinton at the White House.

At the State Department meeting and lunch, there was a full discussion of Israel's plans to build new housing for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem and of economic issues, such as how the Palestinians could attract more private capital to their self-ruled areas.

Earlier, at the White House meeting with Arafat, Clinton criticised Israel's housing plan, saying: "I would have preferred the decision not have been made because I don't think it builds confidence. I think it builds mistrust."
